newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sees 1997 growth of at least 2.3 pct - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sees 1997 growth of at least 2.3 pct - RFTV.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said he was optimistic growth in 1997 would be at least 2.3 percent.

He also said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television broadcast on Monday he was confident France would reduce its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year, as required by the Maastricht treaty.
"We'll respect this objective, three percent deficit maximum," Arthuis said.

The Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development said in its semi-annual economic outlook in December that France would have a deficit of 3.2 percent of GDP in 1997 but could still hit the three percent target by taking new measures.
"The increase (in GDP) will be at least 2.3 percent, that means more tax resources...I'm quite confident and optimistic," Arthuis said.
He also said he saw the rise in unemployment, now running at a record 12.7 percent, peaking in the next few months.
He played down the likely impact of the rise in unemployment on the social security system, which is funded mostly from payroll taxes.

"Our forecasts for the coming year are assessed on the employment forecast, that means we have anticipated the effect of this situation, we don't anticipate a cut in the resources of social security."
The official government forecast for growth in 1997 is 2.3 percent, up from an expected increase of 1.3 percent in 1996.
French national statistics institute INSEE said in December it expected the unemployment rate to hit 13 percent in the spring before starting to decline in the second half of the year.
